plan.title: Feature flag usage on error tracking issues
plan.goal: On an error tracking issue, show which feature flags (and variants) were active on the issue's $exception events, so engineers can spot a flag rollout causing the error. v1 mirrors the existing Releases tab: a new ErrorTrackingIssueFeatureFlagsQuery reads `$feature/<key>` properties off the issue's exceptions in ClickHouse, aggregates occurrences per flag and variant over the preview date range, and enriches the keys with flag id/name/active state through the feature_flags facade so the UI can link to each flag. A new "Flags" tab in the issue filter preview panel renders it, gated by a new ERROR_TRACKING_ISSUE_FEATURE_FLAGS frontend flag. Out of scope for v1: baseline comparison against $feature_flag_called traffic (lift), and flag filters in the issue list.

modules.responsibility: Add ERROR_TRACKING_ISSUE_FEATURE_FLAGS to FEATURE_FLAGS in constants.tsx.
Add NodeKind.ErrorTrackingIssueFeatureFlagsQuery, the query, response and row types; regenerate posthog/schema.py.
Register the ErrorTrackingIssueFeatureFlagsQuery kind in get_query_runner via a lazy import from the error tracking facade.
Export the new runner from queries.py so core query dispatch can reach it, like the other error tracking runners.

New ErrorTrackingIssueFeatureFlagsQueryRunner: aggregates the issue's $exception events by `$feature/<key>` property into per-flag, per-variant counts (capped at N flags), then hands the keys to logic for enrichment. Imports no other product.
New feature_flags.py: resolve_issue_flags(team, keys) maps flag keys to error-tracking-owned IssueFlagInfo(id, name, active, deleted) via the feature_flags facade. Unknown/deleted keys stay unlinked.
queries.ts gains errorTrackingIssueFeatureFlagsQuery builder next to errorTrackingReleasesQuery; the new IssueFeatureFlags logic uses it.
issueFeatureFlagsLogic (loads the query for the preview's issue and date range) and IssueFeatureFlagsPreview (rows per flag with variant split, linking to the flag).
Add a 'Flags' tab to IssueFilterPreviewPanel behind the ERROR_TRACKING_ISSUE_FEATURE_FLAGS flag; clicking a variant adds a `$feature/<key>` property filter to the preview.
Add get_flag_summaries_by_key(team, keys) returning frozen FlagSummary(id, key, name, active, deleted) records, so callers never touch the FeatureFlag model.

seams.rationale: Existing lazy-import dispatch; only the imported names grow.
Same HogQL surface the releases and breakdowns runners already use.
The runner is the only path the query response goes through, so it asks logic for enrichment using error-tracking-owned types.
The only error_tracking→feature_flags edge, owned by business logic and going through the facade, never the models.
Link rows to /feature_flags/:id through the global urls helper; no frontend import of products/feature_flags.
Reads date range and pushes variant filters, same two-way coupling IssueReleases has today.
Panel mounts the tab, as it does IssueReleasesPreview.

comments.author: agent
comments.body: Open decision: v1 reads flag state from the `$feature/<key>` properties the SDKs stamp on $exception events, so it needs nothing from feature_flags except key→id/name enrichment. The alternative is to join posthog.flag_evaluations (gated by is_flag_evaluations_table_enabled in facade/flags.py). That would also catch server-side flags that were never stamped on the event, but it is cloud-only and costs a join. Recommendation: event properties for v1, with evaluations as a follow-up.

resolution.reply: Decided with c2: event properties for v1, flag_evaluations join as a follow-up.

comments.author: human
comments.body: Keep the query runner free of other products. Put the flag enrichment in backend/logic, where issue business logic lives, and route logic -> feature_flags facade instead. Agree on event properties for v1.

resolution.reply: Done. Enrichment now lives in backend/logic/feature_flags.py (resolve_issue_flags returns error-tracking-owned IssueFlagInfo), and logic→feature_flags facade is the only cross-product edge. The runner calls logic for enrichment, because core dispatch sends the query response through the runner. So hogql_queries now depends on logic (a new edge; it doesn't today) but imports no other product. Event properties stay the v1 source.

revisions.note: Initial draft modeled on the ErrorTrackingReleasesQuery + IssueReleases tab path.
